Assumption predicates

Source: R/assumptions-assume.R
Q.Rd

Q holds the predicates of SymPy's Q object, such as Q$positive, Q$integer, Q$invertible or Q$eq. Calling one gives an applied predicate, a boolean expression that prints as in SymPy (Q.positive(x)) and can be combined with &, | and ! and passed to ask(), refine() and assuming(). Asking for a predicate that Q does not have raises an AttributeError; Q$name <- p adds a predicate made with Predicate(), and Q$name <- NULL removes it again.

Usage

Q

Format

An object of class AssumptionKeys.

Details

The predicates are hermitian, antihermitian, real, extended_real, imaginary, complex, algebraic, transcendental, integer, noninteger, rational, irrational, finite, infinite, positive_infinite, negative_infinite, positive, negative, zero, extended_positive, extended_negative, nonzero, nonpositive, nonnegative, extended_nonzero, extended_nonpositive, extended_nonnegative, even, odd, prime, composite, commutative, is_true, the matrix predicates symmetric, invertible, orthogonal, unitary, positive_definite, upper_triangular, lower_triangular, diagonal, fullrank, square, integer_elements, real_elements, complex_elements, singular, normal, triangular, unit_triangular, and the binary relations eq, ne, gt, ge, lt and le.

Examples

x <- Symbol("x")
Q$positive(x)
#> Q.positive(x)
Q$positive(x) & !Q$integer(x)
#> Q.positive(x) & ~Q.integer(x)
Q$eq(x, 1)
#> Q.eq(x, 1)
srepr(Q$positive(x))
#> [1] "AppliedPredicate(Q.positive, Symbol('x'))"
ask(Q$positive(x^2 + 1), Q$real(x))
#> [1] TRUE
